ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus with $AC=8\,\text{cm}$ and $DB=6\,\text{cm}$. If $DH \perp AB$ at H, then what is the length of DH?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, let AC and BD intersect at point O, \\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, AC$=8\text{cm}$, DB$=6\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$AC$\perp$BD, OA$=$OC$=4\text{cm}$, OB$=$OD$=3\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$ $AB=\sqrt{OA^{2}+OB^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}+3^{2}}=5\text{cm}$,\\
$\because$DH$\perp$AB,\\
$\therefore$the area of the rhombus $=AB\cdot DH=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BD=\frac{1}{2}\times 8\times 6=24\text{cm}^{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $DH=\boxed{4.8}\text{cm}$.

method.method_draft: Use an area comparison. First read the diagram: ABCD is drawn as a rhombus, diagonals AC and DB cross at O, and DH is the perpendicular from D to side AB, so DH is the height corresponding to base AB. From the text, take AC = 8 cm and DB = 6 cm. Since a rhombus has perpendicular bisecting diagonals, OA = OC = 4 and OB = OD = 3, so right triangle AOB gives AB = sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = 5. ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, let AC and BD intersect at point O, \\ $\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, AC$=8\text{cm}$, DB$=6\text{cm}$,\\ $\therefore$AC$\perp$BD, OA$=$OC$=4\text{cm}$, OB$=$OD$=3\text{cm}$,\\ $\therefore$ $AB=\sqrt{OA^{2}+OB^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}+3^{2}}=5\text{cm}$,\\ $\because$DH$\perp$AB,\\ $\therefore$the area of the rhombus $=AB\cdot DH=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BD=\frac{1}{2}\times 8\times 6=24\text{cm}^{2}$,\\ $\therefore$ $DH=\boxed{4.8}\text{cm}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is drawn as a rhombus, A and B are below, D and C are above; diagonals AC and DB intersect at point O; from point D a perpendicular is drawn to side AB, with foot H, therefore DH is the height when AB is taken as the base.

Reasoning: It is known that the diagonals of rhombus ABCD are AC = 8 cm, DB = 6 cm. The diagonals of a rhombus perpendicularly bisect each other, so OA = OC = 4 cm, OB = OD = 3 cm. Thus in right triangle AOB, AB = sqrt(OA^2 + OB^2) = sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = 5 cm. The area of the rhombus also equals half the product of the two diagonals, namely S = (1/2) × AC × DB = (1/2) × 8 × 6 = 24 cm^2. On the other hand, DH is perpendicular to AB, so the area also equals AB × DH = 5 × DH. Therefore 5 × DH = 24, obtaining DH = 24/5 = 4.8 cm.
